s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea on exertion in a patient with a history of ovarian cancer and chemotherapy
salient_findings: Elevated Krebs von den Lungen-6 level
Diffuse ground-glass opacity on chest CT
Lymphocytic predominance in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid
key_facts: Diagnosed with stage IV ovarian serous adenocarcinoma 7 years prior
Received TC chemotherapy followed by surgery
Krebs von den Lungen-6 level: 1250 U/mL
Autoantibodies related to connective tissue disease: negative
Total cell count in bronchoalveolar lavage: 615 cells/µL
Diffuse ground-glass opacity on chest CT 15 weeks after initial treatment
Mosaic attenuation and ill-defined centrilobular nodules on chest CT 15 weeks after second treatment

shortlist.label: Chemotherapy-induced pulmonary fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of chemotherapy and symptoms of dyspnea on exertion

shortlist.label: Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: High percentage of lymphocytes in bronchoalveolar lavage and history of ovarian cancer

shortlist.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse ground-glass opacity on chest CT and symptoms of dyspnea on exertion

shortlist.label: Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Bronchoalveolar lavage findings and chest CT results consistent with interstitial lung disease

shortlist.label: Lymphangitic carcinomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of ovarian cancer and symptoms of dyspnea on exertion, with possible metastasis to the lungs

raw.rationale: The patient's bronchoalveolar lavage shows a high percentage of lymphocytes (71%) and the chest CT findings of diffuse ground-glass opacity, mosaic attenuation, and ill-defined centrilobular nodules are consistent with lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia, especially in the context of her history of ovarian cancer and chemotherapy.

rejected.label: Chemotherapy-induced pulmonary fibrosis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of chemotherapy, the lack of specific findings suggestive of pulmonary fibrosis and the presence of lymphocytosis in the bronchoalveolar lavage make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
rejected.why: The patient's chest CT findings do not show the typical pattern of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia, which usually presents with patchy air-space consolidation.

rejected.label: Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
rejected.why: The patient's clinical and radiological findings are more specific and suggestive of lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia rather than the more nonspecific diagnosis of nonspecific interstitial pneumonia.

rejected.label: Lymphangitic carcinomatosis
rejected.why: The patient's history of ovarian cancer could suggest lymphangitic carcinomatosis, but the absence of other specific findings such as pleural effusion and the presence of lymphocytosis in the bronchoalveolar lavage make this diagnosis less likely.
